statement: The canonical readiness-planning snapshot has one identity owner, and that owner VERIFIES rather than assumes: on a miss the planning normalizer builds R = build(P), compares R to P structurally, and grants a canonical entry only when they are content-equal, so a shape whose re-normalisation is not a fixed point never becomes canonical and rebuilds exactly as it does today. This matters because re-normalisation is NOT universally idempotent: over 21600 planning-snapshot shapes (publication status and epoch exhaustive, every other recovery-gate input swept) 15235 shapes — 70.5 percent — diverge, and the narrowest cheap precondition still admits 3405 divergent shapes, so no precondition may stand in for the check. On the seed of a five-node formation, 1430 of 2242 projection calls per 1000 owner builds were re-normalisations of an already canonical snapshot because every producer re-normalised the normalizer's own output and each pass minted a byte-equal copy, defeating the identity memo every downstream planning memo keys on. Identity reuse is gated on the reference identity of every owner the derivation reads (cluster-incarnation fence, system-table cache, membership publication owner); a verified canonical entry is generation-independent because the projection is a pure function of (snapshot, nodeId, fence), while a derived entry stays generation-gated. Entries live in a WeakMap whose self entry holds no reference to its own key, every returned object is frozen, and the caller always receives the freshly built object. Measured on the production-composition rig that matches the live seed within three percent: heavy planning builds fall from 344.8 to 243.6 per second (1218 per 1000 owner builds, minus 29.4 percent) and gate-snapshot builds from 823.6 to 722.4 per second, with publications winner reads unchanged at 824 and no new cache, read, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge or second authority. A shadow audit comparing every served identity against a forced rebuild finds zero divergences over 29811 hits across test/control-plane. That this reduction moves the seed's certification snapshot answer inside the 60 second window is NOT claimed here: it requires the five-node GCP run.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
The canonical planning snapshot has exactly one identity owner: the planning normalizer, which returns the same frozen object for a canonical input rather than minting a byte-equal copy.

Re-normalisation is NOT a universal fixed point (21600 shapes searched, 70.5 percent non-idempotent, and no cheap precondition is sound), so a canonical identity is granted only after the owner verifies at adopt time that build(P) is content-equal to P; a shape that fails verification never becomes canonical and rebuilds exactly as HEAD does.

Identity reuse is gated on the floored planning source generation plus the reference identity of every owner the derivation reads (cluster-incarnation fence, system-table cache, membership publication owner); an entry can never outlive its inputs.

The node-scoped planning memos still read the live publication component and their miss paths build unconditionally, so a publication move without a table write still mints a fresh identity in exactly one rebuild.

No new cache, read, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge, or second ACTIVE or READY authority; publications winner reads stay at 824 and the drain queue keeps maxConcurrency 1 and maxItemsPerDrain 1 with its macrotask scheduler.
Retention is bounded by construction: entries live in a WeakMap, the self entry holds no reference to its own key so no entry can pin the snapshot it describes, and every returned object is frozen.

The measured heavy planning build rate on the shared production-composition rig falls from 344.8 per second to 243.6 per second and must never regress above 1218 builds per 1000 owner builds, and gate-snapshot builds must not regress above 3612; the rate is measured on that rig, never projected.
